title: Replace DateTime.now() wall-clock filler with fixed dates in track_dao_test.dart and track_scoped_dao_test.dart
why: 15 call sites across these 2 files (5 in track_dao_test.dart: lines 116,117,256,297,330; 10 in track_scoped_dao_test.dart: lines 26,44,45,55,56,77,177,203,280,424) use the system wall clock for row timestamps, breaking TQ-6 hermeticity and diverging from every sibling file in this batch, which uses fixed DateTime.utc(2026,...) literals or the drift_memory.dart helper's DateTimeFactory.nowUtc(). None of these values are currently asserted against an exact expected instant, so there is no live flakiness today, but the inconsistency means a future assertion added against 'now' in these files would be non-deterministic where every other DAO test file in the directory is not.
recommendation: Replace DateTime.now()/DateTime.now().toUtc() with fixed DateTime.utc(2026, 1, 1)-style literals (matching the convention in track_dao_delete_test.dart, track_dao_extended_test.dart, etc.) or route through DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() as drift_memory.dart's seed helpers already do.
acceptance_criteria: track_dao_test.dart and track_scoped_dao_test.dart contain no direct DateTime.now() calls for row timestamps.

corrections: The 'diverges from every sibling file' comparison is contradicted by direct grep: at least 9 other DAO test files in the identical directory share the same DateTime.now() pattern.
